verdicts.title: Exact Ramsey Theory: Green-Tao numbers and SAT
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We consider the links between Ramsey theory in the integers, based on van der Waerden's theorem, and (boolean, CNF) SAT solving. We aim at using the problems from exact Ramsey theory, concerned with computing Ramsey-type numbers, as a rich source of test problems, where especially methods for solving hard problems can be developed. In order to control the growth of the problem instances, we introduce "transversal extensions" as a natural way of constructing mixed parameter tuples (k_1, ..., k_m)
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns Ramsey-type numbers (Green-Tao, van der Waerden) and SAT solver benchmarking with encoding schemes, not free-group representation lengths of CNF clause sets or bounds of the form Θ(2^n/log n). It shares the SAT vocabulary but does not interact with the conjecture's specific claim about minimal representation length in a free group.

verdicts.title: Geometric complexity theory and matrix powering
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Valiant's famous determinant versus permanent problem is the flagship problem in algebraic complexity theory. Mulmuley and Sohoni (Siam J Comput 2001, 2008) introduced geometric complexity theory, an approach to study this and related problems via algebraic geometry and representation theory. Their approach works by multiplying the permanent polynomial with a high power of a linear form (a process called padding) and then comparing the orbit closures of the determinant and the padded permanent.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns geometric complexity theory, matrix powering, and lower bounds for the permanent versus determinant problem—it makes no claim about free-group representation length of CNF clause sets or SAT complexity bounds of the form Θ(2^n/log n).

verdicts.title: The relational complexity of linear groups acting on subspaces
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The relational complexity of a subgroup $G$ of $\mathrm{Sym}(Ω)$ is a measure of the way in which the orbits of $G$ on $Ω^k$ for various $k$ determine the original action of $G$. Very few precise values of relational complexity are known.
